Definition: A hash that makes source state explicit so source fidelity can be verified against _REFERENCES.md.
A preserved point-in-time output written as a new timestamped immutable folder that must not be overwritten once accepted.
Mutable convenience pointer metadata that may move; distinct from the durable immutable snapshot folder.
An exceptional, human-approved override of reference hash verification requiring a durable bypass record.
Deliverable-local durable bypass record surface used when a reference hash verification is bypassed.
Specific immutable content evidence (normally a git SHA) to which a human approval binds; required before CHECKING or ISSUED transitions.
A reference source-state in which a file's hash differs from _REFERENCES.md (e.g. REF-006 docs/PRD.md), treated as a warning until reconciliation or acceptance.
Deliverable-local source reference and hash-note surface recording authoritative references and their source state.
A checklist confirming candidate content evidence, approval token/SHA, HEAD recheck before approved actions, and continued human-only authority.
The principle that project state and approvals land in versioned project files and accepted git history, not hidden memory or runtime logs alone.
Previously-considered scope (execution-root validator, dependency graph generator, deliverable lock, unified pipeline run records, staleness propagation) that must not be reactivated.
Project tools and scripts that remain indexed and locally executable when present; exact registry membership remains TBD unless verified.
